oneliner.t: Former two-term Pinal County sheriff (2017–2024) and 2024 U.S. Senate primary runner-up, Trump-endorsed, who won the July 21, 2026 GOP primary for the open AZ-05 seat over Daniel Keenan (about 58.5%) and faces Democrat Elizabeth Lee on Nov. 3.

born.note: Single secondary source (Wikipedia); KTAR gave his age as 53 in Oct. 2025, which is consistent.

hometown.t: Chandler, Arizona (Chandler High School, 1990); spent much of his childhood in Hawaii and also lived in the Philippines, Panama and Argentina

profile.residence_note: His House candidate disclosure lists a primary home in San Tan Valley (Pinal County). In 2026 his family bought a 140-acre ranch in McNairy County, Tennessee; he says he still lives in Arizona (KJZZ). The House requires residence in the state, not the district.

upbringing.t: Born in Hilo, Hawaii, he spent much of his childhood there and also lived in Arizona, the Philippines, Panama and Argentina, graduating from Chandler High School in 1990. He moved to Utah and started a paintball business (Paintball Junkeez) that went bankrupt in 2003, then returned to Arizona and worked in pest control. He spent about six years with the Salt River Pima–Maricopa Indian Community police before joining the Pinal County Sheriff's Office in 2012, and was elected sheriff in 2016. He and his wife Janel have been married since 1994 and had five children; a son, the son's fiancée and their infant daughter were killed in a 2022 Gilbert traffic crash, which he cited when he entered the race. He is a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

platform.t: Credits the Trump administration's crackdown but says a major immigration problem remains; wants to be a strong advocate for the president's policies (Oct. 2025).

Water, Social Security and the economy; says he can work across the aisle.
Traditional values, guns, and a 'national revival of faith, family, freedom.'

promises.t: Be a strong advocate for President Trump's policies in Congress, especially on immigration (Oct. 2025 launch).
Push to ensure only American citizens vote (SAVE Act).

claims.claim: Elected Pinal County sheriff in 2016 and served two terms, not seeking a third.

record.t: Elected 2016 (57.9% general) and 2020 (unopposed on the ballot); served Jan. 2017–Dec. 2024 and was succeeded by Ross Teeple.

claims.claim: Ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 and lost the GOP primary to Kari Lake.

record.t: Finished second with about 39.5% (292,888 votes per Ballotpedia) to Lake's 55.3%.

claims.claim: Says the sexting and misconduct allegations reported by the Arizona Republic are entirely false ('every single bit').

record.t: He did not rebut specific claims. A friend, Matt Hilsabeck, told the Arizona Republic that reports of sexting and conduct outside the marriage were true; about 39 pages of 2020 texts and photos are in county files. The Pinal County Attorney found no criminal conduct but said its review did not address personal-misconduct claims. No court or agency has ruled on the non-criminal allegations.

legal.t: Filed for bankruptcy in Utah when his paintball business, Paintball Junkeez, failed (per his own 2020 book).

His American Sheriff Foundation lost IRS tax-exempt status in May 2021 for not filing returns three years running and stopped filing Arizona annual reports after 2021; the Corporation Commission said in Dec. 2024 it would begin administrative dissolution. Its 2018 sworn state disclosure answered 'no' to a prior-bankruptcy question despite his 2003 bankruptcy; he called it an honest mistake. A 2020 Arizona Republic review found $18,000 of spending unaccounted for in its filings.
legal.status: Revoked (IRS 2021); state dissolution begun Dec. 2024. No charge or official finding on the disclosure answer; Keenan's 'perjury' accusation drew cease-and-desist letters from Lamb's attorney (May 2026).

legal.t: Several women alleged he sent explicit photos and sexually charged messages, and that he used his position to deter them from speaking out. The Pinal County Attorney's Office reviewed the 2020 materials given to the Board of Supervisors plus more than 3 GB submitted in June 2026 and found 'no evidence that Lamb acted in a criminal manner.' A records review also found no documentation of an investigation that a former county attorney said he conducted.
legal.status: Criminal review closed June 2026, no charges. The review covered only whether Arizona criminal law was broken; the personal-misconduct allegations were not adjudicated. Lamb denies them generally.

legal.t: American Oversight (represented by the ACLU) sued Sheriff Lamb and Pinal County in Pinal County Superior Court in May 2024 over five unanswered public-records requests (election-fraud communications, FAIR events, Claremont Institute, 'constitutional sheriffs'). The suit was against his office in its official capacity, not him personally.
legal.status: Official-capacity suit against the office. Wikipedia, citing American Oversight (Dec. 2024), says the office admitted it failed to comply with records law; court terms were not opened.

research_notes: ALLEGATIONS: documented only as follows — (1) allegations of explicit messages/photos to women and of deterring them from speaking out (Arizona Republic, independently verified per Wikipedia citing the Republic and KTAR); (2) a friend's on-record confirmation to the Republic; (3) Pinal County Attorney's closing of a criminal review with no evidence of a crime (scope limited to criminal law). Lamb's campaign attorneys called the claims baseless and Lamb denied them wholesale but did not rebut specifics. Status: no charges, no civil suit found, not adjudicated. FAMILY: Janel Lamb's Facebook statements and the friend's account of encounters with her are her/their records, not his, and are not scored. A son's past drug use (2023 Senate ad) is the son's record. PRIMARY RESULT discrepancy: Wikipedia's AZ House page shows 52,352 votes (58.7%); Lamb's own Wikipedia page shows 43,377 (58.4%/58.5%) — likely different counting dates; certified canvass not opened. Track AIPAC's 'AMP' legend reads 'American Principles' — a human should confirm what that PAC is before publication. Photo not retrieved.
